notes.claim: Unit fractions can be compared and ordered by looking at the denominator: the greater the denominator, the smaller the fraction.
When fractions have the same numerators, the denominators are compared, and the greater denominator gives the smaller fraction.
A common misconception is to compare fractions by whole-number size, judging 1/5 greater than 1/2 because 5 is greater than 2; researchers call this whole-number bias.
The denominator says how many equal parts the whole is divided into, so a bigger denominator means the whole has been cut into more pieces.
